```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

from pathlib import Path
import sys
import zipfile

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

PROJECT_ROOT = Path.cwd()
if not (PROJECT_ROOT / "data").exists():
    PROJECT_ROOT = Path("..").resolve()

sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT_ROOT / "scripts"))
from read_flux_data import read_all_hh

SITE_IDS = ["JP-Ynf", "BE-Bra", "CH-Oe1", "US-MN2", "AU-TTE"]
snapshot_file = sorted((PROJECT_ROOT / "data" / "snapshots").glob("*.csv"))[-1]
snapshot = pd.read_csv(snapshot_file)
site_overview = snapshot[snapshot["site_id"].isin(SITE_IDS)].copy()
site_overview["country"] = site_overview["site_id"].str[:2]
site_overview["site_id"] = pd.Categorical(
    site_overview["site_id"], categories=SITE_IDS, ordered=True
)
site_overview = site_overview.sort_values("site_id")
```

## C2. Data coverage

The measured fraction is the share of half-hours with
`NEE_VUT_REF_QC == 0`. Missing values and quality-control flags are not
counted as measured.

```{python}
#| label: coverage-calculation
#| include: false

all_hh = read_all_hh(PROJECT_ROOT / "data" / "raw")
all_hh["year"] = all_hh["time"].dt.year
coverage = (
    all_hh.groupby(["site", "year"])["NEE_VUT_REF_QC"]
    .agg(share_measured=lambda values: (values == 0).mean())
    .reset_index()
)
coverage["site"] = pd.Categorical(
    coverage["site"], categories=SITE_IDS, ordered=True
)
coverage = coverage.sort_values(["site", "year"])
coverage_matrix = coverage.pivot(
    index="site", columns="year", values="share_measured"
).reindex(SITE_IDS)
best = coverage.loc[coverage["share_measured"].idxmax()]
```

```{python}
#| label: coverage-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Share of half-hours with measured NEE for each site and year."

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 3.5))
image = ax.imshow(
    coverage_matrix.to_numpy(),
    aspect="auto",
    interpolation="nearest",
    vmin=0,
    vmax=1,
    cmap="viridis",
)
ax.set(
    xticks=range(len(coverage_matrix.columns)),
    xticklabels=coverage_matrix.columns,
    yticks=range(len(coverage_matrix.index)),
    yticklabels=coverage_matrix.index,
    xlabel="Year",
    ylabel="Site",
    title="Measured NEE coverage by site and year",
)
plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=45, ha="right")
colorbar = fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax)
colorbar.set_label("Measured half-hours (share)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
print(
    f"The best coverage occurs at {best['site']} in {int(best['year'])}, "
    f"with {best['share_measured']:.1%} of half-hours measured."
)
```

## C3. Summary statistics

The table reports the variables used for the data summary. The missing
percentage is calculated from the half-hourly records. For `P_F`, the mean
column is the mean annual precipitation sum rather than the mean half-hour
value. `GPP_NT_VUT_REF` and `RECO_NT_VUT_REF` are the nighttime-partitioned
products; no separate daytime partitioning was used.

```{python}
#| label: summary-statistics
#| tbl-cap: "Summary statistics for the selected half-hourly variables."

summary_variables = {
    "TA_F": "TA_F (deg C)",
    "SW_IN_F": "SW_IN_F (W m-2)",
    "VPD_F": "VPD_F (kPa)",
    "P_F": "P_F (mm; annual sum)",
    "NEE_VUT_REF": "NEE_VUT_REF (umol CO2 m-2 s-1)",
    "GPP_NT_VUT_REF": "GPP_NT_VUT_REF (umol CO2 m-2 s-1)",
    "RECO_NT_VUT_REF": "RECO_NT_VUT_REF (umol CO2 m-2 s-1)",
    "H_F_MDS": "H_F_MDS (W m-2)",
    "LE_F_MDS": "LE_F_MDS (W m-2)",
}

summary_rows = []
for site, site_data in all_hh.groupby("site", sort=False):
    for variable, label in summary_variables.items():
        values = site_data[variable]
        mean_value = values.mean()
        if variable == "P_F":
            annual_sum = (
                site_data.groupby("year", observed=True)[variable]
                .sum(min_count=1)
            )
            mean_value = annual_sum.mean()
        summary_rows.append(
            {
                "site": site,
                "variable": label,
                "mean_or_annual_sum": mean_value,
                "minimum": values.min(),
                "maximum": values.max(),
                "missing_percent": values.isna().mean() * 100,
            }
        )

summary_table = pd.DataFrame(summary_rows).round(
    {"mean_or_annual_sum": 3, "minimum": 3, "maximum": 3, "missing_percent": 1}
)
summary_table
```

## C4. Daily time series

Daily values are calculated as the mean of the available half-hourly fluxes.
The carbon fluxes are converted from
`umol CO2 m-2 s-1` to `g C m-2 d-1` using the assignment factor 1.0378.

```{python}
#| label: daily-aggregation
#| include: false

carbon_variables = ["NEE_VUT_REF", "GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO_NT_VUT_REF"]
daily_flux = (
    all_hh.assign(date=all_hh["time"].dt.floor("D"))
    .groupby(["site", "date"], as_index=False)[carbon_variables]
    .mean()
)
daily_flux[carbon_variables] = daily_flux[carbon_variables] * 1.0378
```

```{python}
#| label: daily-time-series
#| fig-cap: "Daily NEE, GPP, and RECO for the five selected towers."

fig, axes = plt.subplots(
    nrows=len(SITE_IDS),
    ncols=1,
    figsize=(14, 14),
    sharex=True,
)
for ax, site in zip(axes, SITE_IDS):
    site_daily = daily_flux[daily_flux["site"] == site]
    for variable, label in [
        ("NEE_VUT_REF", "NEE"),
        ("GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "GPP"),
        ("RECO_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO"),
    ]:
        ax.plot(site_daily["date"], site_daily[variable], label=label, linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_ylabel("g C m-2 d-1")
    ax.set_title(site, loc="left")
    ax.grid(True, alpha=0.25)
    ax.legend(loc="upper right", ncol=3)
axes[-1].set_xlabel("Date")
fig.suptitle("Daily carbon fluxes", y=0.995)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

As a check, the daily aggregation for US-MN2 was compared with its
`FLUXMET_DD` file:

```{python}
#| label: daily-cross-check

us_zip = next((PROJECT_ROOT / "data" / "raw").glob("*_US-MN2_*.zip"))
with zipfile.ZipFile(us_zip) as archive:
    dd_name = next(name for name in archive.namelist() if "FLUXMET_DD" in name)
    with archive.open(dd_name) as source:
        daily_reference = pd.read_csv(
            source,
            na_values=[-9999],
            usecols=lambda column: column in ["TIMESTAMP", *carbon_variables],
            dtype={"TIMESTAMP": "string"},
        )
daily_reference["date"] = pd.to_datetime(
    daily_reference["TIMESTAMP"], format="%Y%m%d"
)
daily_reference[carbon_variables] = daily_reference[carbon_variables] * 1.0378
daily_us = daily_flux[daily_flux["site"] == "US-MN2"]
comparison = daily_us.merge(daily_reference, on="date", suffixes=("_from_hh", "_daily"))
for variable in carbon_variables:
    valid = comparison[[f"{variable}_from_hh", f"{variable}_daily"]].dropna()
    difference = (
        valid[f"{variable}_from_hh"] - valid[f"{variable}_daily"]
    ).abs()
    print(f"{variable}: {len(valid):,} overlapping days; "
          f"maximum absolute difference = {difference.max():.4f}")
```

## C5. Diurnal cycles

The mean daily course is calculated by local-standard-time hour. Seasons use
December-February, March-May, June-August, and September-November. For sites
south of the equator, the season names are reversed so that December-February
is summer and June-August is winter.

```{python}
#| label: diurnal-calculation
#| include: false

northern_seasons = {
    12: "winter", 1: "winter", 2: "winter",
    3: "spring", 4: "spring", 5: "spring",
    6: "summer", 7: "summer", 8: "summer",
    9: "autumn", 10: "autumn", 11: "autumn",
}
southern_seasons = {
    12: "summer", 1: "summer", 2: "summer",
    3: "autumn", 4: "autumn", 5: "autumn",
    6: "winter", 7: "winter", 8: "winter",
    9: "spring", 10: "spring", 11: "spring",
}
site_latitudes = site_overview.set_index("site_id")["location_lat"]
all_hh["hour"] = all_hh["time"].dt.hour
all_hh["season"] = [
    (southern_seasons if site_latitudes[site] < 0 else northern_seasons)[month]
    for site, month in zip(all_hh["site"], all_hh["time"].dt.month)
]
```

```{python}
#| label: diurnal-plot
#| fig-cap: "Mean diurnal cycles of NEE and LE by season and site."

seasons = ["summer", "autumn", "winter", "spring"]
diurnal_variables = [
    ("NEE_VUT_REF", "NEE (umol CO2 m-2 s-1)"),
    ("LE_F_MDS", "LE (W m-2)"),
]
colors = {
    site: plt.cm.tab10(index)
    for index, site in enumerate(SITE_IDS)
}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(
    nrows=len(seasons),
    ncols=len(diurnal_variables),
    figsize=(14, 14),
    sharex=True,
)
for row_index, season in enumerate(seasons):
    season_data = all_hh[all_hh["season"] == season]
    for column_index, (variable, axis_label) in enumerate(diurnal_variables):
        ax = axes[row_index, column_index]
        for site in SITE_IDS:
            means = (
                season_data[season_data["site"] == site]
                .groupby("hour", observed=True)[variable]
                .mean()
            )
            ax.plot(means.index, means.values, label=site, color=colors[site])
        ax.set_title(f"{season.title()} - {variable.split('_')[0]}")
        ax.set_ylabel(axis_label)
        ax.set_xticks(range(0, 24, 3))
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.25)
        if row_index == len(seasons) - 1:
            ax.set_xlabel("Hour of day (local standard time)")
        if row_index == 0 and column_index == 1:
            ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize="small")
fig.suptitle("Mean diurnal cycles by season", y=0.995)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## C6. My reading

### Energy balance

For the energy-balance check, only half-hours with measured H and LE
(`H_F_MDS_QC == 0` and `LE_F_MDS_QC == 0`) are used. The tower with the most
valid energy-balance observations is selected automatically.

```{python}
#| label: energy-balance-calculation
#| include: false

energy_columns = [
    "NETRAD", "G_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS_QC", "LE_F_MDS", "LE_F_MDS_QC"
]
energy_data = all_hh.dropna(subset=energy_columns).copy()
energy_data = energy_data[
    (energy_data["H_F_MDS_QC"] == 0)
    & (energy_data["LE_F_MDS_QC"] == 0)
]
energy_data["available_energy"] = energy_data["NETRAD"] - energy_data["G_F_MDS"]
energy_data["turbulent_energy"] = energy_data["H_F_MDS"] + energy_data["LE_F_MDS"]
energy_data = energy_data.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).dropna(
    subset=["available_energy", "turbulent_energy"]
)
energy_site = energy_data["site"].value_counts().idxmax()
energy_site_data = energy_data[energy_data["site"] == energy_site]
energy_slope, energy_intercept = np.polyfit(
    energy_site_data["available_energy"],
    energy_site_data["turbulent_energy"],
    1,
)
```

```{python}
#| label: energy-balance-plot
#| fig-cap: "Energy balance for the tower with the most valid QC-filtered observations."

x = energy_site_data["available_energy"]
y = energy_site_data["turbulent_energy"]
line_limits = [min(x.min(), y.min()), max(x.max(), y.max())]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 6))
ax.scatter(x, y, s=3, alpha=0.12, color="tab:blue", rasterized=True)
ax.plot(line_limits, line_limits, color="black", linestyle="--", label="1:1 line")
ax.plot(
    line_limits,
    energy_intercept + energy_slope * np.array(line_limits),
    color="tab:red",
    label=f"Linear fit (slope = {energy_slope:.2f})",
)
ax.set(
    xlabel="NETRAD - G_F_MDS (W m-2)",
    ylabel="H_F_MDS + LE_F_MDS (W m-2)",
    title=f"Energy balance: {energy_site}",
)
ax.legend()
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Comparison of the five towers

```{python}
#| label: tower-comparison

annual_gpp = (
    daily_flux.assign(year=daily_flux["date"].dt.year)
    .groupby(["site", "year"], observed=True)["GPP_NT_VUT_REF"]
    .sum(min_count=1)
    .groupby("site", observed=True)
    .mean()
)
daily_with_seasons = daily_flux.copy()
daily_with_seasons["month"] = daily_with_seasons["date"].dt.month
daily_with_seasons["season"] = [
    (southern_seasons if site_latitudes[site] < 0 else northern_seasons)[month]
    for site, month in zip(
        daily_with_seasons["site"], daily_with_seasons["month"]
    )
]
seasonal_gpp = (
    daily_with_seasons.groupby(["site", "season"], observed=True)[
        "GPP_NT_VUT_REF"
    ]
    .mean()
)
seasonal_range = seasonal_gpp.groupby("site", observed=True).agg(
    lambda values: values.max() - values.min()
)
mean_measured = coverage.groupby("site", observed=True)["share_measured"].mean()
gap_filled = 1 - mean_measured

highest_uptake_site = annual_gpp.idxmax()
largest_cycle_site = seasonal_range.idxmax()
most_gap_filled_site = gap_filled.idxmax()
least_gap_filled_site = gap_filled.idxmin()

from IPython.display import Markdown, display

display(
    Markdown(
        " ".join(
            [
                f"Using daily GPP as the carbon-uptake measure, {highest_uptake_site} "
                f"has the largest mean annual uptake at "
                f"{annual_gpp[highest_uptake_site]:.1f} g C m-2 yr-1.",
                f"The largest seasonal cycle in mean daily GPP occurs at "
                f"{largest_cycle_site}, with a seasonal range of "
                f"{seasonal_range[largest_cycle_site]:.2f} g C m-2 d-1.",
                f"{least_gap_filled_site} has the smallest average gap-filled "
                f"fraction ({gap_filled[least_gap_filled_site]:.1%}).",
                f"The result that surprised me most was the large gap-filled "
                f"fraction at {most_gap_filled_site} "
                f"({gap_filled[most_gap_filled_site]:.1%}).",
                "The towers represent forest, grassland, cropland, and wetland "
                "ecosystems, so differences in carbon uptake and seasonality are "
                "expected.",
                "The comparison uses NEE_VUT_REF, GPP_NT_VUT_REF, and "
                "RECO_NT_VUT_REF, with the quality flags used to distinguish "
                "measured values from gap-filled values.",
            ]
        )
    )
)
```

## Data and citation

The five site-specific data products and their citations are listed below.
The files are from the ONEFlux v1.3 2026 release and were downloaded with
the FLUXNET Shuttle from AmeriFlux, the ICOS Carbon Portal, and TERN under
the CC-BY-4.0 licence.

```{python}
#| label: site-citations
#| tbl-cap: "Citations for the five site-specific FLUXNET data products."

site_overview[["site_id", "fluxnet_product_name", "product_citation"]].rename(
    columns={
        "fluxnet_product_name": "downloaded_product_file",
        "product_citation": "citation",
    }
)
```

I also cite Pastorello et al. (2020), *Scientific Data* 7, 225:
<https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0534-3>.

> FLUXNET data products were produced and harmonized by eddy covariance
> regional networks and data processing centers, including AmeriFlux,
> ChinaFlux, European Fluxes Database, ICOS, JapanFlux, KoFlux, OzFlux, SAEON,
> and TERN. These products also include a modified version of ERA5 hourly data
> provided by the Copernicus Climate Change Service.
